availability.note: CarExpert MY2027 variant page, released in Australia 5 July 2026; Chasing Cars 22 Oct 2026 says the sedan is 'currently offered in Australia in 200, 220 and 350 trims'. mercedes-benz.com.au configurator returns 403.

listPrice.note: CarExpert MY2027 page: 'prices starting at $72,200' before on-road costs; same figure in CarExpert price-and-specs article ('Price before on-roads' table header) and Chasing Cars review (5 Aug 2026). No price change reported since launch. Manufacturer price list unreachable (403).

batteryKwh.note: usable; EV Database gives 60 kWh nominal, 58 kWh usable for the same variant; CarExpert AU spec also says 58 kWh usable

rangeKm.note: WLTP combined for the AU 18-inch spec; below EV Database WLTP band (542 km TEL / 458 km TEH), so passes the direction test

consumptionKwhPer100km.note: WLTP combined 144 Wh/km (rated, includes charging losses)

bootLitresSeatsUp.note: VDA, rear seats up to the lower window edge (cargo-cover convention); 101 L frunk not added

bootLitresSeatsDown.note: no seats-folded figure published for the sedan (Mercedes quotes 1,290 L only for the Shooting Brake). Scaled 405 × (977/594) from the tesla-model-3 sedan ratio; held 900 had no recorded basis. The wagon ratio (1290/455) would give ~1,150 but a sedan's boot aperture limits it.

towKg.note: CarExpert AU price-and-specs table, braked; EV Database agrees (1500 kg)

warrantyYears.note: 60 months, unlimited km, whole vehicle; battery 96 months/160,000 km

insuranceAnnual.note: kept at held value; anchored to tesla-model-3-long-range-rwd ($61,900, 2550 — Tesla premiums run high), polestar-2-long-range-dual-motor ($71,400, 2200) and mercedes-eqa-250-plus ($86,700, 2250)

depreciationCurve.note: one curve per Mercedes brand by owner convention: matches mercedes-eqa (refreshed 2026-11-26). Steeper than mainstream default on weak Mercedes EV resale (EQA run-out stock at ~$65,490 drive-away against $86,700 RRP).
